Main.sentence: Laurence Henry Tribe (born October 10, 1941) is an American legal scholar known for his studies of ___E:United States constitutional law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_constitutional_law)___ .

Tribe was a professor at ___E:Harvard Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School)___ from 1968 until his retirement in 2020. He currently holds the position of Carl M. Loeb University Professor Emeritus.
A constitutional law scholar,   Tribe is co-founder of the ___E:American Constitution Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Constitution_Society)___ .

He is also the author of American Constitutional Law (1978), a major treatise in that field, and has argued before the ___E:United States Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Supreme_Court)___ 36 times.
Tribe was elected to the ___E:American Philosophical Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Philosophical_Society)___ in 2010.

Tribe was born in 1941 in ___E:Shanghai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai)___ , which was then part of the ___E:Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949))___ but had been taken over by the ___E:Empire of Japan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan)___ in 1937 following the ___E:Battle of Shanghai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Shanghai)___ .
He was the son of Paulina ( née Diatlovitsky) and George Israel Tribe (ne Trejbuch)   His family is Jewish.
His father was from ___E:Poland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland)___ and his mother was born in ___E:Harbin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harbin)___ to immigrants from Eastern Europe.

Tribe spent his early years in the ___E:French Concession of Shanghai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_French_Concession)___ before his family immigrated to the United States when he was six years old.   His family settled in ___E:San Francisco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco)___ , and he attended ___E:Abraham Lincoln High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln_High_School_(San_Francisco))___ .

After graduating from high school in 1958 at age 16, Tribe went to ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ , where he majored in ___E:mathematics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics)___ and was a member of the Harvard Debate Team that won the intercollegiate ___E:National Debate Tournament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Debate_Tournament)___ in 1961.  He graduated from Harvard in 1962 with a ___E:Bachelor of Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ , summa cum laude in mathematics.

Tribe then received a ___E:National Science Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Science_Foundation)___ fellowship to pursue doctoral studies in mathematics at Harvard, but dropped out after one year.  He decided to attend the ___E:Harvard Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School)___ instead, where he was a member of the ___E:Harvard Legal Aid Bureau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Legal_Aid_Bureau)___ .
He graduated from Harvard Law in 1966 with a ___E:Juris Doctor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor)___ magna cum laude .

Tribe married Carolyn Ricarda Kreye in 1964. They divorced in 2008. Their two children, ___E:Mark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Tribe)___ and ___E:Kerry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerry_Tribe)___ , are visual artists.

On May 22, 2013, he was presented with an honorary Doctor of Letters degree from ___E:Columbia University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University)___ during its Class of 2013 ___E:commencement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduation)___ .

After graduating from law school, Tribe ___E:clerked U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_clerk)___ for justice ___E:Mathew Tobriner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Tobriner)___ of the ___E:Supreme Court of California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_California)___ from 1966 to 1967, then for justice ___E:Potter Stewart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potter_Stewart)___ of the ___E:U.S. Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ from 1967 to 1968. He then joined the Harvard Law School faculty as an assistant professor, receiving tenure in 1972. Among his law students and research assistants while on the faculty at Harvard have been former President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ (a research assistant for over two years),  Chief Justice ___E:John Roberts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Roberts)___ ,  US Senator ___E:Ted Cruz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz)___ ,  former ___E:D.C. Circuit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.C._Circuit)___ Chief Judge and ___E:Attorney General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._attorney_general)___ ___E:Merrick Garland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merrick_Garland)___ ,  and Associate Justice ___E:Elena Kagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elena_Kagan)___ .
Other notable students of Tribe were U.S.

Representative ___E:Adam Schiff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Schiff)___ , Chair of the ___E:House Intelligence Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Intelligence_Committee)___ and lead manager for the first ___E:Impeachment of Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_impeachment_of_Donald_Trump)___ ,  and ___E:Jamie Raskin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Raskin)___ , lead manager for the second Donald Trump impeachment.
In 1978, Tribe published the first version of what has become one of the core texts on its subject, American Constitutional Law .
It has since been updated and expanded a number of times.

In 1983, Tribe represented ___E:Unification Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unification_Church)___ leader ___E:Sun Myung Moon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Myung_Moon)___ in the appeal of his federal conviction on income tax charges.

Tribe represented the restaurant ___E:Grendel's Den U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grendel%27s_Den)___ in the case Larkin v. Grendel's Den, Inc. , in which the restaurant challenged a Massachusetts law that allowed religious establishments to prohibit liquor sales in neighboring properties.
The case reached the United States Supreme Court in 1982 and the court overturned the law as violating the separation of church and state.

The Lawyer's Guide to Writing Well criticizes the opening of his brief as a "thicket of confusing citations and unnecessary definitions" stating that it would have been "measurably strengthened" if he had used the "more lively imagery" that he had used in a footnote later in the document.

In the 1985 National Gay Task Force v. Board of Education Supreme Court case, Tribe represented the National Gay Task Force who had won an Appeals Court ruling against an Oklahoma law that would have allowed schools to fire teachers who were attracted to people of the same sex or spoke in favor of civil rights for gay people.
The Supreme Court deadlocked, which left the Appeals Court's favorable ruling in place, declaring the law would have violated the First Amendment.

The Supreme Court ruled against Tribe's client in Bowers v. Hardwick in 1986 and held that a ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ state law criminalizing ___E:sodomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodomy)___ , as applied to consensual acts between persons of the same sex, did not violate fundamental liberties under the principle of substantive ___E:due process U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Due_process)___ .

However, in 2003 the Supreme Court overruled Bowers in Lawrence v. Texas , a case for which Tribe wrote the ACLU's ___E:amicus curiae U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amicus_curiae)___ brief supporting Lawrence, who was represented by ___E:Lambda Legal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambda_Legal)___ .

Tribe testified at length during the Senate confirmation hearings in 1987 about the ___E:Robert Bork Supreme Court nomination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Bork_Supreme_Court_nomination)___ , arguing that Bork's stand on the limitation of rights in the Constitution would be unique in the history of the Court.
His participation in the hearings raised his profile outside of the legal realm and he became a target of right-wing critics.
His phone was later found to have been ___E:wiretapped U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_tapping)___ , but it has never been discovered who had placed the device or why.

Tribe's 1990 book Abortion: Clash of Absolutes , was called "informative, lucidly written and cogently reasoned" in a review in the Journal of the ___E:American Bar Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Bar_Association)___ .
In 1992, Tribe reargued Cipollone v. Liggett Group, Inc. , before the Supreme Court on behalf of Cipollone.

Tribe was part of ___E:Al Gore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore)___ 's legal team regarding the results of the ___E:2000 United States presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election)___ .
Due to the close nature of the vote count, ___E:recounts had been initiated in Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_election_recount)___ , and the recounts had been challenged in court.

Tribe argued the initial case in Federal Court in Miami in which they successfully argued that the court should not stop the recount of the votes which was taking place and scheduled to take place in certain counties.  ___E:David Boies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Boies)___ argued for the Gore team in a related matter in the Florida State Courts regarding the dates that ___E:Secretary of State of Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_State_of_Florida)___ ___E:Katherine Harris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katherine_Harris)___ would accept recounts.
When the original Federal case, Bush v. Gore , was appealed, Gore and his advisers decided at the last minute to have Boies instead of Tribe argue the case at the Supreme Court.
The court determined that recounts of votes should cease and that accordingly George W. Bush had been elected president.
Since the mid-1990s, Tribe has represented a number of corporations advocating for their free speech rights and constitutional personhood.

Tribe represented ___E:General Electric U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric)___ in its defense against its liability under the ___E:Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfund)___ ("Superfund"), in which GE and Tribe unsuccessfully argued that the act unconstitutionally violated General Electric's ___E:due process U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Due_Process_Clause)___ rights.

In 2014, Tribe was retained to represent ___E:Peabody Energy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Energy)___ in a suit against the ___E:Environmental Protection Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency)___ .

Tribe argued that EPA's use of the ___E:Clean Air Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_Air_Act_(United_States))___ to implement its ___E:Clean Power Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_Power_Plan)___ was unconstitutional.

Tribe's legal analysis has been criticized by other legal commentators, including fellow Harvard Law School professors Richard J. Lazarus and Jody Freeman, who described his conclusion as "wholly without merit".
His advocacy for corporations like Peabody has been criticized by some legal experts.

On September 25, 2020, Tribe was named as one of the 25 members of the "Real Facebook Oversight Board", an independent monitoring group over ___E:Facebook U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook)___ .

Tribe is one of the co-founders of the liberal ___E:American Constitution Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Constitution_Society)___ , the law and policy organization formed to counter the conservative ___E:Federalist Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalist_Society)___ , and is one of a number of scholars at Harvard Law School who have expressed their support for ___E:animal rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_rights)___ .
Tribe served as a judicial adviser to ___E:Barack Obama's 2008 presidential campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama%27s_2008_presidential_campaign)___ .
In February 2010, he was named "Senior Counselor for Access to Justice" in the ___E:Department of Justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice)___ .
He resigned eight months later, citing health reasons.

In December 2016, Tribe and notable lawyers ___E:Lawrence Lessig U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Lessig)___ and Andrew Dhuey established The Electors Trust under the aegis of ___E:Equal Citizens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equal_Citizens)___ .

They provide ___E:pro bono U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_bono)___ legal counsel as well as a secure communications platform for those of the ___E:538 members U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_electors,_2016)___ of the ___E:United States Electoral College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College)___ who were considering a ___E:vote of conscience U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unfaithful_elector)___ against ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ in the ___E:presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

After the ___E:dismissal of James Comey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dismissal_of_James_Comey)___ in May 2017, Tribe wrote: "The time has come for Congress to launch an impeachment investigation of President Trump for ___E:obstruction of justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstruction_of_justice)___ ." Tribe argued that Trump's conduct rose to the level of " ___E:high crimes and misdemeanors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_crimes_and_misdemeanors)___ " that are impeachable offenses under the Constitution.

He added: "It will require serious commitment to constitutional principle, and courageous willingness to put devotion to the national interest above self-interest and party loyalty, for a Congress of the president's own party to initiate an impeachment inquiry."

Tribe is on the board of the ___E:Renew Democracy Initiative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renew_Democracy_Initiative)___ , an American political organization founded in 2017 to promote and defend ___E:liberal democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_democracy)___ in the U.S. and abroad.

In 2004, Tribe acknowledged having ___E:plagiarized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plagiarized)___ several phrases and a sentence in his 1985 book, God Save this Honorable Court , from a 1974 book by ___E:Henry Abraham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_J._Abraham)___ .
After an investigation, Tribe was reprimanded by Harvard for "a significant lapse in proper academic practice," but the investigation concluded that Tribe did not intend to plagiarize.
Tribe has stirred controversy due to his promotion of conspiracy theories about Donald Trump's fitness for the presidency.

Dartmouth political scientist ___E:Brendan Nyhan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Nyhan)___ harshly criticized Tribe, saying that he "has become an important vector of misinformation and conspiracy theories on Twitter."  According to McKay Coppins of The Atlantic , Tribe has been "an especially active booster" of the ___E:Palmer Report U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmer_Report)___ , "a liberal blog known for peddling conspiracy theories".
Tribe removed the posted tweets following the Palmer Report and contests the accuracy of the story of controversy.

On August 8, 2023, The New York Times reported that ___E:Kenneth Chesebro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Chesebro)___ , who initially laid out "a plot to use ___E:false slates of electors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_fake_electors_plot)___ to subvert the ___E:2020 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election)___ ", referred to comments by Tribe, to which Tribe responded that his referred comments were "a gross misrepresentation of my scholarship” by Chesebro, and were "taken out of context".

On August 19, 2023, several legal constitutional scholars, including conservative legal scholar ___E:J. Michael Luttig U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Michael_Luttig)___ and Tribe,  argued that former U.S.

President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ is now barred from presidential office under section 3 of the 14th Amendment because of his alleged support for the ___E:January 6 United States Capitol attack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack)___ .

In 2025, Tribe argued that the power that ___E:Elon Musk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk)___ and his ___E:Department of Government Efficiency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Government_Efficiency)___ attempt to exercise over the ___E:U.S. federal government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._federal_government)___ is illegal.
Tribe says that Musk "absolutely" faces a conflict of interest in his roles as a government contractor and federal employee.
